      not think to model is invisible to every arm above -- the classic shape of a control that
      agrees with its author.
  R9. THE PRE-READ IS A NEW DEPENDENCY. The seeder now requires dynamodb:Scan on
      etf-classifications, which it did not need before. It fails CLOSED without it (rc=2, nothing
      written), so the failure is loud rather than silent -- but I did not verify that the identity
      which runs this script actually holds Scan, and an operator who hits that failure and reaches
      for --force-overwrite re-arms the exact revert this cell removed.
  R10. SCOPE. One of three module copies was edited. The other two are off the seeder's import path
      and outside the grant, but "the registry survives a re-seed" is a narrower claim than "the
      classification data is consistent".
  R11. asset_class IS NOT PROTECTED THE WAY management_style IS. 'hedge' is a real value, not a
      placeholder, so the merge writes it; only the conflict refusal stands between a DynamoDB-only
      retag and its reversal, and that refusal is bypassable by a flag. The cell's own sentence --
      "asset_class back to hedge on exactly the rows the retag is about to move" -- is therefore
      answered by an ANNOUNCER, not by an impossibility.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, named so the gap is actionable rather than rhetorical: one run of the new
seeder with --dry-run against the real table under an identity holding Scan, plus a read-back of the
six. That is a live exercise this order's bounds do not grant and I did not take.
